Rule One of the Stork's Questioning Code: When you lock eyes firmly with Elder Stork, you shall be questioned. 
Rule Two of the Stork's Questioning Code: When you avoid Elder Stork's gaze, you shall be questioned.
Rule Three of the Stork's Questioning Code: When you feel you might be questioned, you shall be questioned.
Rule Four of the Stork's Questioning Code: Do not attempt to evade questioning, or you will avert your gaze—refer to Rule Two, and you shall be questioned.
... 
A scholarly journey at the Ink Gate without being "tested" by Elder Stork is no true scholarly journey! 
Regardless of academic performance, anywhere within Ink City, you might be "caught" by an Elder Stork emerging from nowhere and put to the test! And once caught, prepare for at least half an hour of grilling—until you're flushed with embarrassment, seething with frustration, thoroughly roasted inside and out, only then is the "heat" just right. The old man will then close his eyes in contemplation, as if savoring the moment. Only when the aroma of knowledge being baked off you is confirmed will he pat your shoulder and let you go. 
"Let me test you" is like a divine mantra of Ink City, branded into the ears of every disciple, with none spared.
 Elder Stork casts this "divine mantra" not without reason: 
If you don't know, then it's precisely why I should test you—learn through the test, remember deeply, and perhaps you'll grasp it?
If you already know, then why fear my test? A dialogue between teacher and disciple, mutually affirming thoughts, brings even greater benefit. 
If you claim to half-know, all the more reason for me to test you, helping you fill gaps and resolve doubts.
Though often left with smoke rising from their heads and sweat pooling at their feet, disciples emerge as if steamed in a hot spring, feeling strangely clear-headed. Upon reflection later, they often gain new insights. 
Thus, Elder Stork's "tests" have cultivated a mix of love and dread among them.
Being tested is just part of the ordeal—consider it sweating out toxins or enduring stone therapy. Though it may leave you dizzy and gut-wrenched in the moment, the benefits eventually outweigh the pain. 
On the flip side, imagine a day when even Elder Stork no longer wishes to "test you"—now that would be truly terrifying! 
Fortunately, to this day, in all of Ink City, not a single soul has been spared Elder Stork's questioning.
